title: Min Stack With Minimum Count
description:
Design a stack `CountMinStack` that supports standard stack operations plus querying both the current minimum value and how many times that minimum value appears in the stack — all in `O(1)` time.

Implement the `CountMinStack` class:
- `CountMinStack()` initializes an empty stack.
- `void push(int val)` pushes `val` onto the stack.
- `void pop()` removes the top element of the stack.
- `int top()` returns the top element of the stack.
- `int getMin()` returns the minimum value currently in the stack.
- `int getMinCount()` returns the number of elements in the stack equal to `getMin()`.
constraints: Methods pop, top, getMin, and getMinCount are always called on non-empty stacks.
At most 5 * 10^4 calls will be made across all methods.
hints: Store (val, curMin, minCount) at each stack level — or keep a secondary stack of [minVal, count] pairs.
On push(val): if val < curMin start count at 1; if val == curMin increment count; if val > curMin carry over (curMin, minCount).

examples.explanation: After pushing [4, 2, 5, 2], minimum is 2 with count 2; popping 2 drops count to 1; popping 5 and 2 leaves [4] with min 4 and count 1.
Pushing three 7s yields min 7 with count 3.
When a strictly smaller value -1 arrives, min becomes -1 with count 1; popping it restores the previous minimum and count.
